evidence_quotes.quote: This article analyzes the procedural progress of three public civil actions related to basic sanitation filed in the Municipalities of Aquidauana, Mato Grosso do Sul; Tubarão, Santa Catarina and Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul.
A seleção desses três casos foi aleatória já que o presente trabalho se insere em uma pesquisa mais ampla que visa a acompanhar todas as 258 ações.

The conclusions reached were as follows: (i) there is a great chasm between the judicial consecration of the law and its effective implementation in reality; and (ii) the courts' websites do not contain information about the actual enforcement of court decisions in the cases examined.

No caso de Aquidauana, o processo foi extinto 12 anos após o ajuizamento da ação, sem que fosse realizado o cumprimento do determinado em sentença. A empresa Sanesul, responsável pela prestação dos serviços, limitou-se a juntar aos autos um projeto de lei que regulamentaria a prestação dos serviços pelos próximos 30 anos.

Já em Santa Maria, apesar de fora do prazo inicialmente estipulado, o cumprimento da obrigação ocorreu três anos e meio após o início da fase de execução. Finalmente, no Município de Tubarão, o projeto executivo que deveria ter sido elaborado no prazo máximo de 1 ano, foi apresentado somente em agosto de 2016, mais de 5 anos após a sentença. Já a implementação do sistema de esgoto, que, segundo determinação judicial, já deveria ter sido realizada, não ocorreu sequer em parte.

effect_estimate.comment: Primary analysis of the 3 cases is qualitative/descriptive based on docket tracking and secondary press/utility records; background statistics from the first author's 2014 study of 258 lawsuits (79.69% granted, 4% implemented by 2013, 0% on time) are also cited in the Introduction for context.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across 3 randomly selected public civil actions ordering sanitation/sewerage provision (drawn from a prior dataset of 258 sanitation lawsuits in which 79.69% were granted but only 4% had been implemented by 2013 and 0% within court-ordered deadlines), all 3 won favorable rulings with court-set deadlines and daily fine threats (R$ 1,000/day in Santa Maria; R$ 500/day in Tubarão), yet none complied within the judicially established deadlines: (1) Aquidauana (filed 1999): first-instance judgment took 10 years and 5 months plus ~1 year on appeal, and execution was closed/archived in 2011-2012 as fulfilled after the utility (Sanesul) merely filed a 30-year municipal concession bill, despite actual sewerage coverage standing at 15% in August 2011; (2) Santa Maria (filed Dec 2006): judgment took <6 months plus ~1.5 years on appeal, and CORSAN completed the street sewerage network enabling residential connections in December 2012 (3.5 years into execution, missing the August 2010 court deadline and 10 years after residents' 2002 administrative complaint); (3) Tubarão (filed 2006): judgment took 5 years and 2 months plus 4 years and 8 months on appeal, the executive project ordered within 1 year was completed only in August 2016 (>5 years post-sentence), 0% of the sewerage system had been implemented as of writing, and initial works only began in March 2018 (12 years after filing) covering 3 of 23 neighbourhoods (<37% of the 104,457 inhabitants). Court websites lacked full case-file access and contained no reliable records on actual enforcement.
